The hulls of warships from three separate fleets and three separate eras layer the same stretch of dark, each generation of dead ships drifting through the bones of the last.
A dense shoal of destroyer-sized hulks spins through the field in a slow shared tumble, their hulls interleaved and tangled as though they died in a mass collision and never separated.
Dead warships hang nose-down toward a dead star in a vast loose cluster, drawn slowly inward by faint residual gravity, a graveyard that will eventually feed itself to a cold sun.
A battle-line of snapped capital ships stretches kilometres across the dark, each hull broken at the keel and folded open, the silent evidence of a broadside engagement nobody survived to report.
Wrecks encrusted with ice hang in a frozen shoal, every hull-breach sealed by centuries of accumulated frost, the whole graveyard glittering pale and silent like some vast cold jewel-box of the dead.
The hollow shells of orbital stations and the warships that failed to defend them drift together in a slow mixed field, the ruins of an entire defended position reduced to cold debris.

Gutted warship hulls have been slowly colonised by drifting asteroid debris, stones and metal fused together into strange composite hulks, the ships no longer entirely ships but not yet entirely rock.
